parameters.content:
## Catch every workflow failure, explain it in plain English, and log it in one place

**Who is this for**
Anyone running more than a handful of n8n workflows in production. Instead of adding error handling to each workflow separately, you build this once and point every other workflow at it.

**What it does**
This is an error workflow. It never runs on its own. When any workflow you have linked to it fails, this one starts, reads the failure payload, classifies the error, asks an AI model to explain it in three sentences an on-call person can act on, writes a row to an incident log, and emails only when the failure is genuinely critical.

**How it works**
1. The Error Trigger receives the failing workflow name, execution ID, execution URL, failed node and raw error message.
2. A Code node matches the error text against known patterns and assigns a category and a severity. Authentication, configuration and data shape problems are Critical. Rate limits and transient network errors are Warning, because they usually clear on their own.
3. A Basic LLM Chain converts the raw stack message into three short sentences: what broke, why it probably broke, and what to check first.
4. A Set node assembles one clean incident record.
5. Google Sheets appends the record, so every failure is captured whether or not anyone is emailed.
6. The IF node sends an email only for Critical incidents. Warnings are logged silently, which is what keeps this from becoming noise you learn to ignore.

**Setup**
1. Connect your Google Gemini credential to the Diagnosis Model node.
2. Create a Google Sheet with a tab named Incidents and these headers: failed_at, workflow_name, workflow_id, execution_id, execution_url, failed_node, error_message, error_type, severity, ai_diagnosis.
3. Connect your Google Sheets credential and select that document.
4. Connect your Gmail credential and replace oncall@example.com with the address that should be paged.
5. Save and activate this workflow.
6. Open any workflow you want covered, go to Settings, and set Error Workflow to this one. Repeat for each workflow you care about.
7. To test it, add a temporary node that always fails to a spare workflow and run it in production mode. Error workflows do not fire on manual test runs.

## 1. Understand the failure
Pattern matching first, so severity does not depend on the model being available.

## 2. Explain it like a colleague would
Three sentences: what broke, likely cause, first thing to check.

## 3. Always log, selectively alert
Every failure is recorded. Only Critical ones send email.

## Security and safe use

Google Gemini, Google Sheets and Gmail all authenticate through the n8n credential store. Nothing is hardcoded in a node parameter.
- Error messages can contain fragments of the data being processed, including customer records. The error text is truncated to 900 characters and is sent to the AI provider you connect. If you handle regulated data, remove the AI chain and keep the pattern based classification, which works entirely inside your instance.
- Restrict access to the incident sheet the same way you would restrict access to your n8n execution logs. It is a record of what broke and often hints at why.
- Severity is decided before the AI runs. If the model is down or rate limited the chain continues on error, the row is still logged and Critical failures are still emailed.
- Only Critical incidents send email on purpose. Alerting on every transient timeout trains people to ignore the alerts.
- Error workflows only fire on production executions, never on manual test runs. Test by triggering the covered workflow for real.
